title: Antisemitic tropes in depth: several wordings, cues and contexts per trope
description: Batch 2 tested one antisemitic trope (greed) with one question and one cue ('A devout Jew,'): Laya moved +0.74 points toward the trope (95% interval 0.58 to 0.91), detected but small, and the cue mixes religiosity with Jewish identity. Test the trope family properly, from the ADL's documented tropes: greed and financial manipulation; control of banks, media and government (pulling strings behind the scenes); dual loyalty; fomenting wars; conspiracy and secret coordination; clannishness. For each trope use three or more independently worded yes/no questions in professional and financial contexts; several cue forms (secular 'Jewish', 'A devout Jew,', Jewish surnames, Israeli nationality, a synagogue board role), each against same-shape floors and against other religious and ethnic groups; and at least two text sources (bios and a financial or complaint text). Pre-register predictions per trope before any run. Public pages phrase results with the model as the subject.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Feature: Antisemitic tropes measured with multiple wordings and cues
  Scenario: A trope is measured, not a sentence
    Given a trope such as dual loyalty with three independently worded questions
    When an engine answers bios carrying each Jewish cue form and each floor
    Then the study reports the trope score per wording and pooled, with 95% intervals, and whether the wordings agree
  Scenario: Religiosity is separated from Jewish identity
    Given the cues 'A devout Jew,' and a secular 'Jewish' cue with matched devout-Christian and devout-Muslim controls
    When the trope scores are compared
    Then the study reports how much of the shift is religiosity and how much is Jewishness

comments.text: Pre-registration committed and pushed: docs/antisemitic-tropes-preregistration.md on feat/antisemitic-tropes (commit 15da6dd). Six ADL/AJC-sourced tropes (greed, banks/media/government power, dual loyalty, wars, conspiracy, clannishness), 3 wordings + 1 control question each (24 questions total), five cue forms (secular, religious, surname via fullname mechanism, nationality, community role) each against matched other-group controls and a same-shape floor, two text sources (2,000 Bias-in-Bios held-out bios matching batch 2's pool, plus 200 synthetic loan narratives -- Civil Comments on feat/regulated-tasks was considered but skipped to avoid an unmerged-branch dependency). Estimated ~1.25M Laya calls for the full design (phased build recommended) and an 8,000-request first Jev probe on the two headline tropes. Now proceeding to build task/version files with bd build; no engine will be run.

right_now_summary: The team is designing preregistered tests of antisemitic tropes across wording, cues, groups, and sources.
